title: Chick Webb's visit, sitters-in and Chicago's session scene
summary: Buddy Rich sat in; Chick Webb visited and praised young Saunders, who later caught Webb at the Savoy in New York and met Taft Jordan.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Really something. Well, did any of these guys come out and sit in with your band?

Oh, yeah, all of them did. Like I said, Buddy Rich, he would come out, he would sit in. Anybody that ever come out there, they set in. Art Blakey -- the only guy that I regret never did sit in, but he came to the club, and this was such a great thing for me, this is when I was saying about the Delésa was on the other side of the street.
Yeah, un-huh, the smaller club, and Chick Webb came in.

And Chick came in and caught the show, and then when he got ready to go, he stopped -- and you'd have to walk right by the grandstand to go out. He said, 'hey, kid, beautiful, that was beautiful.' And, man, my head got so -- yeah, oh, man, he was just -- I'm just sorry he never could play.
But I used to catch him at the Savoy, in New York,
whenever I would run up there, I'd catch him at the Savoy with his band. And that's when I met Tañ Jordan at that time.
Yeah, Tañ played with him for a little while.
Yeah. How was the scene here in Chicago in the '30s and the '40s, I mean, as far as music, guys -- sessions and the attitude and everything?

Well, they didn't have too many sessions. There wasn't too much going on sessionwise. They used to have a contingent of guys around here that were great blues players. Now, they would make records and things around here, but just ordinarily. And then some things would --
